build: release, debug symbols, offline locked dependencies
methodology: Three sequential process runs; each operation has nine calibrated batch timing samples, each targeting approximately 12 ms. Report median of the three batch medians.
Warm operations exclude fixture creation and file IO; include destruction of returned results. First reads measured separately in fresh processes, excluding process startup and input file IO.
Allocation counters enabled separately from timing. Allocated bytes are cumulative requested allocation sizes, not RSS. Peak and retained bytes count heap allocations made during this operation only.

Same RX bytes for digests on/off. Off path retains normalization, semantic validation, reference bounds/cycle checks, digest widths, and normal PAC/record decoding. Only digest preparation/calculation/comparison is skipped.
Prepared SHA-256 inputs exactly match per-member structural hash inputs. This microbenchmark excludes preparation and the final bundle digest.
Reused-meta experiment builds the same embedded Prescription once outside timing; still decodes and verifies the full RX every time. No decoded user Definition cache.

Established-runtime baseline uses unchanged current compiled-layout implementation on matching scalar field names/widths. Different format and validation workload: not a drop-in runtime integration comparison.
New native RX record-runtime integration is not implemented. These are Definition load/verification measurements, not per-event decode/render or end-to-end Snoot performance.
All experimental reader changes are isolated under /tmp; no library behavior changed.

Untouched production source control compiled separately and measured in three subsequent sequential runs. Benchmark refactoring changes code generation slightly; retain control results separately rather than attributing that difference to digests.
interpretation: Digests remain required. Digest-off measurements are diagnostic baselines only. Reused-meta measurements reuse only the embedded meta-definition prescription, not decoded user definitions; all digests remain verified in the verified variant.
